paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The LORD of Hosts is holy, and Isaiah shows that holiness meeting a stack of woes: grabbing more until you "live alone in the land," chasing the next drink, calling "evil good and good evil," and taking bribes that deprive "the innocent of justice" (Isaiah 5:8, 11, 20, 23). Different woes, one root, because these folks "rejected the instruction of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel" (Isaiah 5:24). When you stop listening to God's Word, everything else starts to bend.

The party crowd had music at every feast, but they "fail to see the work of His hands" (Isaiah 5:12). Then some of them say, "Let Him hurry and hasten His work so that we may see it!" (Isaiah 5:19). You can be busy, loud and comfortable, and still be looking right past God.

So here's what we carry out of this one. "The LORD of Hosts will be exalted by His justice, and the holy God will show Himself holy in righteousness" (Isaiah 5:16). That's why Isaiah says the anger of the LORD burns against His people and "His hand is still upraised" (Isaiah 5:25), and it's why we don't treat His Word like a side dish. Let it shape what you call good, what you call bitter, and who you listen to.
